newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps upgrades Cooper debt, paper.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps upgrades Cooper debt, paper.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Wednesday it upgraded its debt ratings of Cooper Industries Inc because of a stable business outlook and an improved debt-to-capital ratio.

The senior unsecured debt rating has been raised to Single-A from Single-A-Minus, 6.0 percent debt exchangeable for common stock is raised to Single-A from Single-A-Minus, 7.05 percent convertible subordinated debentures are increased to Single-A-Minus from Triple-B-Plus and commercial paper has been raised to D-One from D-One-Minus, Duff & Phelps said.
The upgrades affect about $1 billion in debt securities.

Duff & Phelps attributed the upgrades to more financial flexibility after Cooper's debt-to-capital ratio returned to its targeted range. Duff & Phelps said the company's diverse product and market mix, efficient manufacturing and consistent cash flow support the ratings.

"DCR anticipates, however, that Cooper's improved financial flexibility will result in increased efforts to make strategic acquisitions and/or make share repurchases under an existing $275 million authorization, limiting further credit improvement," Duff & Phelps said.
Cooper is a diversified manufacturer of electrical products, automotive products and tools and hardware.
